subject: OrbitAI renewal: dedicated capacity resize proposal
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitai.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing — sustained higher utilization ahead of renewal

Hi David,

Quick note from OrbitAI — our Q2 traffic pattern continued into July. We’re seeing a steady 45–55% higher token throughput versus the baseline we used when signing last year. P99 latency has crept up a bit during peak windows (we saw a few spikes to ~1.1s for our 2k-sequence workloads).

We’re approaching our renewal window and want to understand options for:
- adding a small tranche of GPUs for guaranteed headroom, or
- resizing the pool (different GPU mix) to reduce cost per token while keeping P99 latency below 900ms, or
- a staged commit tied to utilization thresholds.

Could you share a recommendation and a rough SOW so procurement can review? I attached the last two months of usage exports.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform
OrbitAI

Attachments: OrbitAI_usage_Jun-Jul2026.csv (csv)
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing — sustained higher utilization ahead of renewal

Elena — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We pulled the file into our sizing model and ran a short analysis. High-level takeaways:

- Your 7am–11am UTC window shows consistent 50% higher token volume vs. baseline; average GPU utilization there is ~78% on the current tranche.
- Tail latency (P99) is sensitive to concurrent long sequences; those correlate to a small set of endpoints routing large-batch gen jobs.

Two viable paths from our side:
1) Staged top-up: add 6 A100-equivalent slots now as a burst tranche with autoscale to permanent after 60 days if utilization stays >= 70%. Estimated incremental monthly spend: $33k.
2) Reprofile + mix change: migrate 30% of your slot hours to cheaper L40s with micro-quantization and a cache hot-path for short responses — target p99 ~850ms with ~12% cost reduction.

I’d like Ben to weigh in on operational routing and Marissa to draft a starter SOW. Can we do a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to walk this through with procurement?

Best,
David
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing — sustained higher utilization ahead of renewal

Looping in ops notes from a quick test run:

- If we add 6 A100-equivalent slots behind your existing routing policy, average queue wait drops immediately for the peak window; sustained cost impact is predictable.
- The L40-mix approach requires a small model variant (FP16 -> 4-bit quant) validation for OrbitAI prompts; we can run a 72-hour quality check using a sample prompt set from the customer.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache would give you a ~6–9% effective token reduction for short-chat endpoints; that helps the reprofile option the most.

Operational caveats: SLO gating during transition — we recommend a canary route (5% traffic) for the first 48 hours and auto-fallback to the existing fleet if p99 rises >100ms from baseline.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitai.com>, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-06T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed SOW and pricing scenarios (OrbitAI renewal)

Hi Elena — attaching a starter SOW and two pricing scenarios:

Scenario A — Immediate burst tranche (recommended if you want zero-risk latency guardrail):
- 6 A100-equivalent reserved slots (burst pool) for 3 months, convert to dedicated reserve if utilization >= 70% over 60 days.
- One-time onboarding fee: $4,000.
- Estimated monthly delta: $33,000.

Scenario B — Reprofile + commitment optimization (recommended if you want cost efficiency):
- Migrate up to 30% of committed slot-hours to L40-equivalent with quantization profile tested in a 72-hour QA window.
- Implement prefix/KV caching and routing policy tweaks.
- One-time QA and validation: $6,500.
- Estimated monthly delta: $28,900 (plus potential token efficiency savings).

I’ve attached SOW_orbitai_dedicated_resize_v1.docx and a short P99 analysis (latency_p99_report_Q2.pdf). If you want, we can include a clause that ties conversion to long-term reserved capacity to a utilization audit (we’ll ingest your metrics through our billing + telemetry integration).

Next steps: confirm preferred scenario and sign the SOW. I can convert to a DocuSign link once we lock terms.

—Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_orbitai_dedicated_resize_v1.docx (docx), latency_p99_report_Q2.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitai.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Ravi Singh <ravi@orbitai.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SOW and pricing scenarios (OrbitAI renewal)

Thanks — we reviewed both options internally with procurement and infra. Quick answers:

- Favor Scenario B if the QA run does not show >3% drop in generation quality for our top 50 prompts. Procurement is OK with a utilization-audit conversion clause.
- Please kick off the 72-hour QA and share the exact sample prompt set (we’ll provide it via shared Drive).
- Can you add a 30-day termination notice to the staged conversion clause (procurement request)?

If QA looks good we’ll sign and expect the reprofile migration to start in mid-September. Please send a DocuSign once the SOW reflects the termination language.

Best,
Elena
